hunks.baseline: At the voice that pierced my ear, I lifted my gaze from the smartphone I had been staring at.
The face that appeared countless times in the articles was standing right in front of me.
hunks.sol: At the voice in my ear, I looked up from my phone. The face I’d seen in countless article photos was right in front of me.

hunks.baseline: Amid thunderous applause and enthusiastic support, he had become Ares Guild’s new captain. Now he asked with a calm expression:
hunks.sol: Now Ares Guild’s new captain, welcomed with applause and cheers, Team Leader Choi regarded me calmly.

hunks.baseline: “What are you looking at so intently?”
hunks.sol: “What are you looking at?”

hunks.baseline: “Articles about Team Leader Choi. No, should I call you Guild Master now? Or Vice Guild Master? You’ve got one foot in each Guild, so it’s confusing.”
hunks.sol: “Articles about you. Should I still call you Team Leader Choi? Or Guild Master now? Maybe Vice Guild Master? You’ve got a foot in each Guild. It’s confusing.”

hunks.baseline: “Call me whatever you prefer.”
hunks.sol: “Whatever you’re comfortable with.”

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. Should I? Minwoo?”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. How about Minwoo?”

hunks.baseline: “Ah… Please just call me Guild Master Choi Minwoo.”
hunks.sol: “Ah… Guild Master Choi Minwoo would be fine.”

hunks.baseline: “That feels awkward. I’ll just keep calling you Team Leader.”
hunks.sol: “That feels awkward. I’ll stick with Team Leader.”

hunks.baseline: Considering the people’s gazes and the position he held, Guild Master would have been the proper title.
hunks.sol: Given his position and the people watching, Guild Master would have been the proper title. But he couldn’t refuse my suggestion. It was a hundred times better than *Minwoo*.

I crossed the familiar hallway while muttering inwardly.
This was where I had fought a fierce battle against the mutated Go Jun. As a result, every direction I looked and every path I followed was filled with wreckage.
hunks.sol: I crossed the familiar hallway. I’d fought the mutated Go Jun here, and wreckage littered everywhere I looked and stepped.

hunks.baseline: The problem was that Team Leader Choi and I had to search the entire place with a fine-toothed comb.
hunks.sol: And Team Leader Choi and I had to comb through it.

hunks.baseline: No. Strictly speaking, there were three of us.
It was just that the other member wasn’t human.
hunks.sol: Well, not just the two of us. Our third member wasn’t human.

hunks.sol: “Are my eyes playing tricks on me? I could’ve sworn you said you’d take me to a club. You promised drinking games with beautiful women.”

And then…
*When I came back.*
*He was running away.*

hunks.baseline: At the time, Go Jun had been fleeing in that horrible form—a creature made from a mixture of human and monster.
hunks.sol: By then Go Jun had changed into a horrible mixture of human and monster. He’d definitely been fleeing.

hunks.baseline: But the important question was where he had been heading.
hunks.sol: The question was *where* he’d been going.

hunks.baseline: *That’s it. There’s something there that I failed to find.*
hunks.sol: *That’s the place. There’s something there I didn’t find.*

hunks.baseline: Without another thought, I launched myself forward.
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King hurried after me as I shot ahead like the wind.
hunks.sol: I launched myself forward without another thought. Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King hurried after me as I shot ahead like the wind.

hunks.baseline: It was a place we had already searched several times.
But this time, something was different.
hunks.sol: We’d searched the place several times already, but this time was different.

hunks.baseline: There was a dead-end hallway and several rooms.
hunks.sol: A dead-end hallway. Several rooms.

hunks.baseline: I slowed down and pressed myself against the wall, heightening my Qi Sense.
hunks.sol: I slowed and leaned close against the wall, heightening my Qi Sense. A System chime sounded, and a blue circle spread outward from me.

hunks.baseline: With a chime from the System, a blue circle spread outward from me.

hunks.baseline: But even after searching every corner of the hallway and rooms, no notification appeared to tell me that I had found anything.
hunks.sol: It swept the hallway and every room, but no notification appeared to tell me I’d found anything.

hunks.baseline: The range of [Qi Sense] was determined by the System, and I could perceive only as far as that range allowed.
hunks.sol: The System determined the range of my Qi Sense. I could perceive only what lay within it.

hunks.baseline: But was that truly all there was?
hunks.sol: But was that really all?

hunks.baseline: I calmly regulated my breathing.
The sounds around me receded, and the internal energy rising from my dantian lent strength to my Qi Sense.
hunks.sol: I steadied my breathing. The sounds around me receded, and internal energy rose from my dantian, lending strength to my Qi Sense.

hunks.baseline: And then…
At the moment my Middle Dantian finally responded—
hunks.sol: And then, at the moment my Middle Dantian finally responded—

hunks.baseline: The blue circle that had stopped expanded outward.
hunks.sol: The blue circle, which had stopped expanding, surged outward. Beyond the space I could see, toward another space hidden from sight.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the visible space, toward another space hidden in secret.
At the very edge of its reach was the notification I had been waiting for.
hunks.sol: At the edge of its reach came the notification I’d been waiting for.
